subject: geography
title: KS3 Geography - Weather and Climate
subtitle: Weather processes, climate patterns, data skills and climate change responses.
description: A KS3 Geography revision pack covering weather and climate definitions, weather measurement, rainfall processes, pressure systems, UK weather patterns, climate graphs, global climate zones, extreme weather and climate change responses. The content is grounded in the supplied study pack and designed for repeated retrieval practice.

data.title: How Clouds and Rainfall Form
data.instruction: Put the rainfall formation steps in the correct order.
items: Water evaporates from seas, lakes, rivers and soil.
Warm air holds water vapour.
The air rises and cools.
Water vapour condenses into tiny droplets.
Clouds form as droplets gather.
Droplets grow larger and fall as precipitation.

data.title: Relief Rainfall in the Western UK
data.instruction: Put the relief rainfall sequence in the correct order.
items: Moist south-westerly air travels from the Atlantic Ocean.
The air reaches western uplands such as Wales or the Lake District.
The air is forced to rise over high land.
Rising air cools and condensation forms clouds.
Rain falls on the windward side of the hills.
Air sinks on the leeward side and becomes drier.

data.title: Convectional Rainfall
data.instruction: Put the convectional rainfall sequence in the correct order.
items: The Sun strongly heats the ground.
The ground warms the air above it.
Warm air rises because it is less dense.
The rising air cools.
Water vapour condenses to form clouds.
Heavy showers or thunderstorms may fall.

data.title: Enhanced Greenhouse Effect
data.instruction: Put the human-caused warming sequence in the correct order.
items: People burn fossil fuels, farm intensively and remove forests.
Extra greenhouse gases enter the atmosphere.
More outgoing heat is trapped by the atmosphere.
Average global temperature rises.
Wider climate patterns, sea levels and extreme weather risks can change.

data.title: Weather or Climate?
data.instruction: Sort each statement into weather or climate.

Cloud cover reached 8 oktas this afternoon.
Polar regions are very cold for most of the year.
One storm affected the town last night.
Rain falls in every month on average in a temperate maritime climate.
